summary: Iteration-6 deployment-fix verification: 11/11 backend tests PASSED in /app/backend/tests/test_deploy_fix.py. All acceptance criteria from the review met. (1) GET /health (NO /api prefix) on the backend pod (localhost:8001, i.e. the k8s probe path that was 404ing) returns HTTP 200 with body {"status":"healthy"} in ~1ms. (2) GET /api/health returns 200 {"status":"healthy"} both on the pod and via the public ingress. (3) GET /api/ still returns 200 with {message:'ReHairAnalytics API', status:'ok'}. (4) POST /api/scan with 3 real fixture JPEGs completes end-to-end via public URL: real gpt-5.6-terra analysis, all metrics in 0-100, ai_summary >20 chars, region='full', frames_analyzed=3, storage_path='rehairanalytics/uploads/...'; images retrievable via GET /api/files/{path} (200, image/*, >500 bytes, thread-offloaded get_object). (5) Batched _attach_children CORRECTNESS: GET /api/sessions and GET /api/timeline both return the created session with exactly 3 attached images (all with matching tracking_session_id) and analysis object (also matching tracking_session_id) - no cross-session contamination from the single $in query. (6) EVENT-LOOP RESPONSIVENESS proved: while a real 2-frame /api/scan was in flight, a background thread polled GET /health on localhost every 300ms; ~28 polls all returned 200 in <2s each (backend log shows a continuous stream of 200 OK /health responses interleaved with the concurrent LiteLLM gpt-5.6-terra calls, then finally 'POST /api/scan HTTP/1.1 200 OK'). asyncio.to_thread wrapping of store.put_object/get_object and image_utils.process_image/make_thumbnail/to_base64_jpeg is working - the loop is not blocked. AI features verdicts: POST /api/scan (gpt-5.6-terra via EMERGENT_LLM_KEY) - pass; Emergent Object Storage put/get - pass. Skills loaded: ai-testing-core (LLM output was checked via analysis['ai_summary'] length + metric ranges; specialist skill not needed since text output is short server-generated summary).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: root-level @app.get('/health') at line 33 and @app.get('/api/health') at line 38 are declared BEFORE app.include_router(api_router) and outside the /api prefix - correct for the k8s probe.

_attach_children (lines 253-266) correctly uses a single $in query over the full page of session ids for both images and analysis and groups them into dicts keyed by tracking_session_id - N+1 removed, verified by the 3-images-per-session correctness check.

auto_scan (line 375): store.put_object, image_utils.process_image, image_utils.to_base64_jpeg, image_utils.make_thumbnail are all wrapped in asyncio.to_thread. upload_image, analyze_session, and download_file are similarly wrapped. Verified empirically by the concurrent /health poll test.

Minor: /api/scan still opens 6 concurrent LLM calls per request via asyncio.Semaphore(6). Under production burst load this could still exhaust the OpenAI RPM/TPM (not blocking, but 500-worthy) - a per-user rate limit would be defensive.

Minor: auto_scan reads uploaded files sequentially in an async for-loop with `await f.read()` before dispatching threads - fine for the 2-3 frames typical case but for 36 frames the read stage is serialised. Not a deploy blocker.

Minor: /api/auth/session (line 158) still uses the synchronous `requests` library inside an async route (`http_requests.get(EMERGENT_SESSION_URL, ...timeout=30)`). This is another sync-in-async call that can block the loop. It was NOT part of the iteration-6 fix but is architecturally the same class of bug the review targeted; consider httpx.AsyncClient or asyncio.to_thread here as well.
test_credentials: Seeded fresh MongoDB user + session_token in test_database via class-scoped fixture 'deploy_user'; auth via Authorization: Bearer <token>. Cleaned up on class teardown.
seed_data_creation: One temp user test-user-deploy-<ts>-<rand> and its session_token created and deleted per test class run (see fixture).
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_deploy_fix.py is the regression suite for the deployment fix. Run with: `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<public-url> pytest /app/backend/tests/test_deploy_fix.py -v`. It expects the backend to be reachable both on http://localhost:8001 (for the k8s probe path /health check) AND at the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (for /api routes). If you re-run, do NOT use `-s` with the pre-configured `-n 2 --dist loadscope` xdist config - xdist worker stdout multiplexing gives spurious failures when capture is disabled. Just run without -s (or add `-n 0` to serialize).
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of the deploy 404: the k8s liveness/readiness probe hits GET /health on the backend pod (port 8001) but every route in server.py was under APIRouter(prefix='/api') so there was no /health handler at the root - FastAPI returned 404 and the pod was flapping. Nginx 'upstream timed out' during heavy /api/scan was a secondary symptom: the request handler called sync store.put_object (requests) and Pillow image ops directly in the async loop, so while a scan was running the loop could not answer any other request (including /health), causing the ingress to time out. FIX (already applied by main agent): (a) added @app.get('/health') and @app.get('/api/health') registered on the top-level app before include_router - both now return {"status":"healthy"}; (b) wrapped every blocking storage + Pillow call in auto_scan/upload_image/analyze_session/download_file with asyncio.to_thread so the loop stays responsive; (c) collapsed N+1 image/analysis lookups in /api/sessions and /api/timeline into a single $in batched query via _attach_children. VERIFIED: /health returns 200 in <2ms on localhost:8001, /api/health returns 200 via public URL, and 28 concurrent /health polls all returned 200 during an in-flight /api/scan. No re-test needed.
